solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The fellow needing rest, worker reluctant to get going

parts.note: a male person is HE
to rest in a chair is to sit
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A tired labourer, wanting a sit-down, is slow to start the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hesitant holds back and is slow to commit to action.

clue.text: From an Italian city, motorway leading to roads east

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords
lanes are minor roads
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Directions out of an Italian city: take the motorway, then the roads heading east.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes people or things belonging to Milan, the Lombard city.

clue.text: Flier, enthusiast that can go round and round, up or down

definitions.text: that can go round and round, up or down

parts.note: a wing is what flies, so a flier in the sense of an aerofoil
a nut is a fanatic, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: A keen pilot is described as spinning about in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: In politics a wing nut is also a crank, but here the definition is the fastener with two flat lugs, turned by hand up or down a bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A threaded fastener with wings for the fingers is spun along a bolt in either direction.

clue.text: Mineral store almost completed on time

indicators.note: something almost completed lacks its final part, so the store word loses its last letter

parts.note: to garner is to gather and store up

explanation.surface: A shop full of minerals is nearly finished, right on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the time piece to the end of GARNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Garnet is a silicate mineral, often deep red and used as a gemstone.

clue.text: Red-top offering faithful representation!

definitions.meaning: the Daily ... is a British tabloid, one of the papers with a red masthead
a true reflection or image of something

explanation.surface: A tabloid paper claims to offer a truthful picture of events.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Mirror is a red-top tabloid, and a looking glass gives an exact image.

clue.text: Rain, snow, hail? Hurry!

definitions.meaning: examples of water falling from the sky
rash haste, as in acting with undue speed

explanation.surface: A forecaster urges people to get inside before the weather turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorologists use the word for all falling water, and it also means headlong haste.

clue.text: Roll a large map out — it's very unlikely to be square

definitions.text: it's very unlikely to be square

indicators.note: letters put out of their order are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Unrolling a big map flat, someone notes it is hardly ever a neat square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ROLLALARGEMAP. The definition is fair because a square is technically one, but almost never.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-sided figure with opposite sides parallel is only square in the special case of equal sides and right angles.

clue.text: Naturalist not working for heritage organisation

indicators.note: letters set working are put into action in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An off-duty naturalist volunteers for a conservation body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges NATURALISTNOT. The National Trust is a British charity that cares for historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The British charity preserves historic buildings, gardens and landscapes for the nation.

clue.text: Plant a cairn untidily

indicators.note: something done untidily is jumbled up, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone sets a plant beside a carelessly piled heap of stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidily' rearranges CAIRN into RNICA, after A taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnica is a mountain flowering herb whose extract is used for bruises.

clue.text: Produce energy that's half wasted in fireplace

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a grate holds the fire in a fireplace

indicators.note: half of the word's letters are thrown away, leaving its first half

explanation.surface: Half the heat produced is lost up the chimney from an open fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half wasted' leaves ENE from ENERGY; 'in' puts it into GRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to bring something into being, as a power station produces electricity.

clue.text: Grandmother who can be got around

indicators.note: a word you can go round either way reads the same from both ends

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A grandmother is described as easy to talk round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nan is an informal British word for one's grandmother.

clue.text: Name of a square youngster affecting upper-class attitudes

definitions.meaning: a ... Ranger, a fashionable young person of posh west-London style

explanation.surface: A posh young person is named after a London square.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloane Square in Chelsea gave its name to the Sloane Ranger, a young person with upmarket airs.

clue.text: Beyond rule with riot spreading

indicators.note: a riot spreading scatters, so these letters are dispersed into a new order

explanation.surface: A riot spreads past the point where rules can contain it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulterior first meant lying on the further side, so beyond.

clue.text: Age of Cockney goddess

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: Hera is queen of the Greek gods

explanation.surface: Someone asks how old a goddess is, in an East End accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class London accent, famous for dropping initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of history, as is an age.

clue.text: Guy may be kept in place by this

definitions.text: Guy may be kept in place by this

parts.words: Guy may be kept in place by this
parts.note: Guy looks like a man's name, but a guy is the rope that braces a tent

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what keeps a man called Guy where he is.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy ropes holding a tent upright are anchored to the ground by spikes driven into it.

clue.text: Writer producing short piece of verse

indicators.note: a short version is cut off at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a poem is a piece of verse

explanation.surface: A writer turns out a brief poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgar Allan Poe was the American author of tales and poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was an American author of macabre stories and verse.

clue.text: Unfortunately philosopher has no time for one like Palin

parts.note: alas is an expression of regret

indicators.note: a word that has no letter loses it

parts.note: Immanuel Kant was the German philosopher

explanation.surface: Sadly a great thinker lacks the leisure to meet a famous politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarah Palin was Governor of Alaska.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah Palin, former governor of the state, is a native of it, so one like her comes from there.

clue.text: Prisoner at back of boat? This may help if he goes overboard!

definitions.text: This may help if he goes overboard!

parts.note: a lifer is a convict serving a life sentence
aft means towards the stern of a vessel

explanation.surface: A convict stands at the stern, and something may save him if he falls off.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable rescue craft keeps a person afloat after leaving a ship in an emergency.

clue.text: Cleaners who may cadge things off others?

definitions.meaning: things used to wipe and wash surfaces

definitions.text: who may cadge things off others
definitions.meaning: people who scrounge from others without paying

explanation.surface: The household cleaning staff are suspected of scrounging.
explanation.definitionFit: Absorbent cleaning pads and freeloaders who live off others share the same word.

clue.text: Paddington's welcoming gesture?

parts.note: Paddington could be the London station, but he is the famous children's-book bear, and his embrace would be one of these

explanation.surface: Someone imagines how the famous storybook animal would greet a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight, enveloping embrace is named after the way an animal of Paddington's kind would hug.

clue.text: Don't allow wastage of jam

definitions.meaning: to save or preserve something rather than squander it

explanation.surface: A frugal cook warns not to throw away any jam.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to keep from waste, and the noun is a fruit preserve.

clue.text: Old Bob doesn't have casual trousers

parts.note: bob was slang for a shilling, the old British coin abbreviated S
to lack something is not to have it

explanation.surface: An elderly man named Bob turns up without his comfortable trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was the shilling, a British coin before decimalisation in 1971, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose informal trousers are called by this plural noun.

clue.text: The woman served up awful tea put in the microwave again?

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up has the word going upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: her refers to a woman

indicators.note: an awful version is a mangled one, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman offers a dreadful cup of tea that has been zapped twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns HER into REH; 'awful' rearranges TEA into EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Warming food a second time, often in a microwave, is the verb meant.

clue.text: Unfriendly father at the front of old hovel

indicators.note: one piece is placed before the rest

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
a sty is a filthy dwelling

explanation.surface: A priest stands frostily at the door of a run-down shack.
explanation.definitionFit: A frosty manner is cold and unwelcoming.

clue.text: One voting in favour indeed

definitions.meaning: a yes vote, or the person casting it
an old or dialect word for yes, certainly

explanation.surface: A supporter of the motion agrees emphatically.
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament the ayes vote yes, and the word itself is a dialect yes.

clue.text: Gill's one pause for rest

definitions.meaning: a gill is an organ that breathes for a fish, so it is one that breathes
a short break to catch one's breath

explanation.surface: Someone called Gill takes a short break.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish's gill is literally one that takes in air, and a short rest lets you get your breath.

clue.text: Relish added to artist's stew

indicators.note: the first piece comes after the second

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword's usual artist
gout is the French for taste or relish

explanation.surface: A painter spices up a casserole with sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: Goût is French for taste, used in English as relish.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a highly seasoned stew of meat and vegetables.

clue.text: What DIYer must do to accommodate rabbit — don't hang about!

definitions.text: What DIYer must do to accommodate rabbit
definitions.meaning: a home handyman would construct an enclosure for the pet

explanation.surface: A home handyman must build a hutch for the pet in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means build a pen for a pet; idiomatically it means flee quickly.
